chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Billy Eckstine's band with Gene Ammons at the Plantation
summary: The interviewer raises the bebop pioneers in Teddy Hill's and Calloway's bands; Horace recalls Eckstine's swinging band with Gene Ammons and the record 'I Love the Rhythm of a Riff'.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah. That's always a word to get around. Yeah. The reason I was asking is that I was -- you've mentioned Cab Calloway, of course, and Teddy Hill a number of times, and I brought up Billy Eckstine. In the late '30's and early '40's some of the musicians who later were the major innovators of bebop were involved in those bands,
like Dizz Gillespie was playing in Teddy Hill's band, and Cab Calloway for a period of time, and Billy Eckstine had one of the great, really, jazz bands for a short period of time at that time.

You know, I was going to say that. You know, Billy had a great jazz band, and he played out in Los Angeles at a club, what we talked about earlier, called the Plantation, out at 108th and Central Avenue, and he had a saxophone player in his band who I think we might say had a little name, Gene Ammons, Jug.
Man, he was playing. You know, Billy was playing a little trumpet and trombone on him too.

Yes. And so he had a swinging band. I remember recording. I've got it here now, 78, and the name of the tune was 'I Love the Rhythm of a Riff.' And 'I love the rhythm of a riff, ta-tee-ta-ta-tee-ta-ta-tee-ta,' and, man, he was swinging, and then Jug would come in behind him. That's all she wrote, you know. It was a great band he had. Oh, yes.
